artifact_schema.description: A sealed bound record, schema ecbench.bound/v1, as aburan28/crypto's ecbench writes it (docs/bounds/README.md there), with every non-integer number carried as its shortest round-trip decimal string, because cairn's canonical encoding has no floats (tools/bound_artifact.py render writes one from the record). A worked example is cairn/checkers/fixtures/prime-rho-neg.artifact.json, rendered from a byte copy of a committed record, which scores 682064; prime-bsgs-neg.artifact.json scores 866743.

bound_id.description: ECBND1h followed by 12 hex digits: the SHA-256 of the record's bytes with this field empty.

domain.description: problem ecdlp.single_target, family prime, target_kind planted, unit ecbench.gae, tier toy, envelope one cold target without precomputation.

sizes.description: One row per curve: slug, r, field_bits <= 32, automorphisms_available, floor_s, runs == verified > 0, mean_gae, mean_s, ratio_to_floor; every stated figure recomputes from the counts.

constant.description: ratio_to_floor.value equals the run-weighted mean of the sizes' ratios.

dimensions.description: ops.known true and ops.value equal to constant.ratio_to_floor.value.

provenance.description: sessions named by directory, session id and the SHA-256 of records.jsonl; verified equal to the sum over sizes.

statement: Stage 2 of docs/cairn-integration-plan.md: the measured frontier of the ecdlp.single_target problem on prime-field curves with planted targets, in the ecbench.gae unit (group-addition equivalents, the whole method, cold, one target), at the toy tier (fields of at most 32 bits). An artifact is a sealed bound record (aburan28/crypto docs/bounds/README.md, schema ecbench.bound/v1) fitted by ecbench from an audited session. The pinned evaluator recomputes every size's S = mean_gae / sqrt(r) and its ratio to the generic floor sqrt(pi / 2A) from the record's own counts, the pooled ratio from the sizes, the tier from the field sizes and the domain from its fields, and scores the parts per million of the floor achieved: 1000000 at the floor, higher is closer. A record that disagrees with itself, measures time, lies outside this domain or tier, or is not admissible scores 0, which the threshold of 1 rejects; the evaluator never raises, so a bad record is a rejection and not an outage. The ratchet starts at 500000 (a method spending twice the floor's group additions) and ends at the floor itself, so the verifier's threshold decides whether an artifact is a bound record and the ratchet decides whether it moves the frontier; a slow but self-consistent method is accepted and pays nothing. The evaluator cannot verify that the named sessions exist and replay -- that is the measuring repository's CI (ecbench bound check, ecbench verify --replay-all) and an independent receipt cited by hash in the record -- so an accept here is a receipt for a well-formed, self-consistent frontier entry and backs no direction in this program's ledger on its own (invariant b). reward is 0, and so is the ratchet's pool: nobody outside this program funds it yet, and the frontier is the point, not the payout. One objective is one domain and one tier (invariant d): another domain is a copy of the evaluator with other constants, hence another hash, hence another objective.
